result:
I used to think freedom meant having no constraints. An empty calendar, an open road, no expectations. Now I think freedom is the ability to choose which constraints to keep.

There is a quiet that happens at 5 a.m. The city hasn't decided what it wants to be yet. The buses are asleep. My coffee cools too fast because I keep staring at streetlights blinking off one by one. In that hour I can write anything, delete everything, and not owe an explanation to anyone.

People ask what I’m working on, and I say I’m figuring it out. That is both a lie and the truth. I am working on patience, which is a word for learning how to stay in a room with an unfinished thought.

I have a plant on my windowsill that I keep forgetting to water. It leans toward the light anyway. I find that comforting. It is doing the best it can with what it is given, and it does not apologize for the tips on its leaves.

Maybe that is the whole thing. We are all leaning toward something. Work, love, a better version of ourselves we can't describe. Some days the light is harsh and we wilt. Some days it is enough.

I don’t need an empty calendar. I need one with white space to breathe, and enough appointments to remind me I am alive. Freedom, I think, is not the absence of walls. It is knowing which wall you want to paint.

There is a quiet that happens at 5 a.m. The city hasn't decided what it wants to be yet. The buses are asleep. My coffee cools too fast because I keep staring at streetlights blinking off one by one. In that hour I can write anything, delete everything, and not owe an explanation to anyone.

People ask what I’m working on, and I say I’m figuring it out. That is both a lie and the truth. I am working on patience, which is a word for learning how to stay in a room with an unfinished thought.

I have a plant on my windowsill that I keep forgetting to water. It leans toward the light anyway. I find that comforting. It is doing the best it can with what it is given, and it does not apologize for the tips on its leaves.

Maybe that is the whole thing. We are all leaning toward something. Work, love, a better version of ourselves we can't describe. Some days the light is harsh and we wilt. Some days it is enough.

I don’t need an empty calendar. I need one with white space to breathe, and enough appointments to remind me I am alive. Freedom, I think, is not the absence of walls. It is knowing which wall you want to paint."
